profile.reading: LightEdge Austin II sits in Austin, Texas, though LightEdge own site publishes two distinct Austin addresses, 2916 Montopolis Drive and 7000-B Burleson Road, with an unresolved discrepancy between LightEdge own pages over the Burleson Road building suite number and zip code, and no source reviewed this session could confirm which specific address corresponds to this record Austin II designation as opposed to the separate Austin I record elsewhere in this dataset. Per LightEdge own combined specification sheet for the Austin market, the facility or facilities together provide 2.5 megawatts of critical IT load and 8.25 megawatts of generator capacity with an isolated 2N UPS configuration, across 58,471 total square feet including 40,960 square feet of white space. The facility carries a broad compliance-oriented certification set common across LightEdge portfolio, including SOC 1, 2, and 3, ISO 27001, 20000-1, and 22301, HITRUST, HIPAA and HITECH readiness, and PCI DSS, with nine on-net carriers including AT&T, Cogent, Lumen, Zayo, and Spectrum. LightEdge Solutions was founded in 1996 and is headquartered in Des Moines, Iowa. LightEdge announced a new partnership with GI Partners, a private equity and real estate investment firm that also created Digital Realty in 2004, in September 2021, and underwent a CEO transition from longtime leader Jim Masterson, who led the company 21 years, to Rob Carter effective January 1, 2025. LightEdge describes its current footprint as 20 data centers across 12 US metro markets plus a location in Amsterdam, Netherlands. No tenant is named for this facility, and no year-built or tier-rating figure is disclosed for the Austin market on LightEdge own site. Austin has grown rapidly as a Texas technology hub over the past decade, drawing both large hyperscale campuses from other operators and mid-market colocation demand of the kind LightEdge compliance-focused business model typically serves, consistent with the company decision to maintain two separate buildings in that specific metro.

reading.body:
LightEdge Austin II is a data center in east Austin whose published power capacity and square footage are not available on the operator's public spec page. The facility ranks 19th among Texas sites with published megawatt figures, and the state hosts 133 mapped data centers of which only 18 have disclosed capacity to this research site.

Without published IT load or power specifications, the campus cannot be assessed for its role in AI scaling or ranked against other facilities competing for grid resources in Texas. The operator has chose to withhold capacity details from its public materials, requiring direct contact to determine whether this site carries material weight in the state's compute infrastructure.

The absence of published specifications places LightEdge Austin II outside the basis for comparative analysis of grid constraints on AI deployment. For a reader weighing where compute capacity will concentrate, this campus remains unquantified.
